content: pigz does NOT parallelize decompression (man page: decompression cannot be parallelized without specially prepared deflate streams); it only parallelizes compression via byte-aligned concatenated deflate chunks. True parallel inflate of arbitrary gzip requires speculative deflate-block boundary discovery plus 32KiB LZ77 window reconstruction (rapidgzip, arXiv 2308.08955); block finders produce false positives that must be validated by trial decode. RFC 1952 concatenated multi-member gzip is legal and decoders must process ALL members - single-member-only decoding silently reads a prefix (real-world soci-snapshotter bug; rustkmer itself hit this, fixed in commit 8102985 with MultiGzDecoder + regression test). Cheap safe wins: file-level parallelism across split parts, member-level parallelism, and producer/consumer overlap of decompression with counting.
